\section{Release Status}\label{release-status}

This is the canonical editable QMD source for the Tools engineering
design manual. It is a governance scaffold, not a released engineering
manual. The file-level module inventory is complete for its declared
tracked-source denominator. TOOLS-D4 registers one model-conditioned
D-plane calculation and one swing/Rate-of-Closure textbook exemplar with
exact source, consumer, test, fixture, equation, unit, and limitation
traceability. The markerless-mocap exemplar remains explicitly blocked
because its authority PR is unmerged and no markerless module exists on
this exact source base. Release remains blocked by TOOLS-D5 through
TOOLS-D9 and outstanding D4 approvals. Generated HTML, LaTeX, PDF, and
DOCX artifacts are reproducible engineering records under TOOLS-D2, but
none is approved for publication or engineering use.

\section{Documentation Authority and Release
Boundary}\label{documentation-authority-and-release-boundary}

\subsection{Purpose}\label{purpose}

The manual will explain shared calculations and interchange contracts
from theory and assumptions through typed inputs, units, coordinate and
time conventions, algorithms, implementation symbols, tests,
uncertainty, limitations, consumer surfaces, and artifacts. Tools source
and evidence remain authoritative; the manual cannot approve a
calculation that its owning source, evidence, license, or human review
has not approved.

\subsection{Canonical Source}\label{canonical-source}

Only QMD under \texttt{manuals/tools} is editable manual source.
Existing user guides, ADRs, package documentation, generated API
references, and publications are separate governed products. They can
supply reviewed references, but none is a second mutable source for this
manual.

Generated LaTeX, PDF, DOCX, and HTML are non-editable artifacts. A
correction starts in canonical QMD, then regenerates every affected
representation through the qualified toolchain. TOOLS-D2 owns that
toolchain; TOOLS-D7 and TOOLS-D8 own artifact review and publication
evidence.

\subsection{Evidence and License
Classes}\label{evidence-and-license-classes}

Every calculation and claim must be classified as observed, derived,
model-scenario, external, provisional, unavailable, or approved within
an explicit scope. Every borrowed source and generated artifact must
preserve its license and attribution. Content from Tools\_Private or
another non-public source may not enter this public manual without
explicit public authority.

\subsection{Approval and Failure
Semantics}\label{approval-and-failure-semantics}

The default is deny-until-approved. Missing inventory coverage, source
authority, units, coordinate or time convention, implementation symbol,
test, validity range, uncertainty, license, artifact digest, page
review, accessibility review, or human approval keeps the affected item
blocked. Unsupported values are never replaced with synthetic or
plausible values without an explicit model-scenario contract.

\subsection{Exemptions}\label{exemptions}

Freshness failures are release-blocking. The TOOLS-D1 module baseline is
recomputed from tracked implementation and governed configuration files
by
\texttt{python\ -m\ scripts.build\_tools\_module\_inventory\ -\/-check};
later TOOLS-D6 work must extend freshness from the file baseline to
stable calculation pathways. Future exemptions must be structured,
narrowly scoped, justified, owned, reviewed, and expiring. An exemption
cannot authorize an equation, scientific claim, artifact, operating use,
license transfer, or public projection.

\subsection{Current Boundary}\label{current-boundary}

TOOLS-D1 establishes a complete file-level denominator for its declared
tracked scope. TOOLS-D2 establishes deterministic byte reproduction and
governed semantic preservation across HTML, LaTeX, PDF, and DOCX. Its
generated artifacts remain non-editable and unapproved. The conservative
inventory does not establish stable calculation identity, equation
correctness, validity ranges, uncertainty, page/accessibility approval,
or publication authority. TOOLS-D4 registers one model-conditioned
D-plane exemplar with explicit equation-to-code-to-test evidence while
retaining review-required inventory authority. The markerless-mocap
exemplar remains fail-closed because its source dependency is unmerged.
Expansion, executable freshness, review, publication, and human approval
remain blocked under TOOLS-D5 through TOOLS-D9.

\section{Module and Calculation-Candidate
Inventory}\label{module-and-calculation-candidate-inventory}

\subsection{Purpose and Denominator}\label{purpose-and-denominator}

\texttt{manifests/module-inventory.json} is the deterministic TOOLS-D1
index for every tracked implementation source file and governed
configuration module in the repository. It scans recognized Python,
Python stub, JavaScript, TypeScript, Rust, MATLAB, C/C++, Arduino,
shell, PowerShell, HTML, CSS, Prisma, JSON, YAML, TOML, INI, XML, URDF,
and web-manifest files. Tests are evidence inputs rather than
implementation rows. Generated, vendored, archived, experimental,
example, documentation, resource, and manual trees are excluded
explicitly in the manifest, so a consumer can reproduce the exact
denominator. The index binds bounded entry shards by normalized SHA-256,
contiguous index, entry count, and first/last path. Both the index and
every shard remain below the repository's one-megabyte file budget;
consumers reassemble one logical view only after verifying every shard
and the exact declared shard set.

At this baseline, 3,439 modules are classified: 808 conservative
calculation candidates and 2,631 non-calculation modules. One legacy
JavaScript file has a non-UTF-8 encoding and remains explicitly blocked
rather than being decoded by an implicit platform default. These counts
describe inventory coverage only; they are not test coverage,
calculation approval, or publication readiness.

\subsection{Deterministic Identity and
Integrity}\label{deterministic-identity-and-integrity}

Each file receives a provisional path-derived identifier and a SHA-256
digest of normalized text bytes. The normalization maps CRLF and bare CR
to LF before hashing. For module path (p\_i) and normalized content
digest (h\_i), the tree authority is

\[
H_{\mathrm{tree}} = \mathrm{SHA256}\left(
  \Vert_{i=1}^{n} p_i : h_i
\right),
\]

where rows are ordered by normalized repository-relative path. This
contract makes the result independent of Windows checkout line endings
while retaining content changes. The path-derived identifier is not a
stable calculation ID; TOOLS-D3 owns the structural chapter contract;
TOOLS-D4 owns exemplar registration and stable equation-to-code
identities that survive file movement.

\subsection{Classification Contract}\label{classification-contract}

A module is a \texttt{calculation} candidate only when its normalized
path contains a governed calculation marker, such as dynamics,
kinematics, pressure drop, signal processing, geometry, solver, energy,
force, or trajectory, or when the source imports a recognized scientific
mathematics library. All other modules are \texttt{non-calculation}.
This intentionally conservative static screen can have false positives
and false negatives, so every calculation candidate has
\texttt{authority\_status=provisional} and
\texttt{review\_status=review-required}.

The inventory also records language, purpose where statically available,
maintainer family, public surfaces and routes, mapped tests and
validation, ADRs, equation references, literal units, citations,
artifact digests, risk tags, normalized byte count, and content digest.
Missing tests, sources, units, chapters, equation pathways, validation,
routes, or artifact digests remain \texttt{unavailable},
\texttt{not-applicable}, or explicitly pending their owning subepic;
they are never synthesized. Non-calculation status means only that the
conservative detector found no calculation signal. It does not waive
public-API, security, licensing, accessibility, or downstream
compatibility review.

\subsection{Consumer and Failure
Contract}\label{consumer-and-failure-contract}

The repository-owned schema is
\texttt{schemas/module-inventory.schema.json}, version
\texttt{tools-module-inventory/1.0.0}. It extends the program-owned
calculation registry without copying or competing with that shared
schema. Both JSON Schema validation and the Python consumer reject
unknown fields, unsupported versions, unsafe paths, invalid hashes,
duplicate identifiers, unsorted duplicate traceability arrays,
denominator mismatches, and unsupported state values.

Any tracked in-scope module addition, removal, rename, or normalized
content change makes inventory check mode fail until the manifest is
regenerated and reviewed. A green inventory check proves only
deterministic classification and freshness of this file-level baseline.
Public projection remains blocked until the remaining stable-pathway,
page, accessibility, licensing, publication, and human-approval gates
are complete.

\section{Reproducible Rendering
Contract}\label{reproducible-rendering-contract}

\subsection{Outcome and Authority}\label{outcome-and-authority}

TOOLS-D2 renders the canonical QMD into deterministic HTML, LaTeX, PDF,
and DOCX representations. Generated outputs are engineering records, not
approval. Only QMD may be corrected directly. Every output remains
blocked from public projection until semantic, page, accessibility,
provenance, licensing, and human-review gates owned by later subepics
are complete.

The renderer uses the pinned command versions and inputs recorded in
\texttt{toolchain-lock.json}. It verifies the exact first version line
before render, expands only bounded QMD includes, uses the governed
bibliography and reference DOCX, disables TeX shell escape, normalizes
volatile package metadata, and binds every representation into
\texttt{manifests/artifacts.json}. The command model follows the
documented Pandoc conversion contract (Pandoc contributors 2026) while
QMD remains compatible with the pinned Quarto authoring surface (Posit
Software, PBC 2026).

\begin{figure}
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.7\linewidth,height=\textheight,keepaspectratio,alt={Deterministic rendering pathway.}]{figures/render-pipeline.png}
\caption{Deterministic rendering pathway.}
\end{figure}

\subsection{Semantic, Unit, and Warning
Preservation}\label{semantic-unit-and-warning-preservation}

The semantic contract is deliberately format-neutral. Every
representation must retain the governed title, release boundary,
representative unit string, warning, figure label, and bibliography
identity before receiving a shared semantic digest. Example unit string:
10 m/s.

WARNING: Provisional calculations remain blocked.

This gate proves preservation of required meaning across the four
representations. It does not prove calculation correctness, equation
coverage, accessibility, page aesthetics, or release approval. Missing
text, a stale digest, an unpinned tool, an unsafe include, or an absent
artifact fails closed.

\subsection{Reproduction and Consumer
Contract}\label{reproduction-and-consumer-contract}

Run
\texttt{python\ -m\ scripts.render\_tools\_design\_manual\ -\/-verify-toolchain}
before a qualified build. Run
\texttt{python\ -m\ scripts.render\_tools\_design\_manual\ -\/-render}
to replace renderer-owned artifacts, then
\texttt{python\ -m\ scripts.render\_tools\_design\_manual\ -\/-check} to
validate source, toolchain, byte, and semantic bindings. The strict JSON
Schemas allow consumers to validate the lock and manifest without
importing producer code.

Artifact rows expose media type, byte count, byte digest, and shared
semantic digest. The manifest also preserves the owning epic, review
owner, explicit blockers, and a null immutable source commit while this
local stack is not a merged authority. A consumer must reject unknown
fields, versions, formats, paths, hashes, status promotion, or semantic
divergence.

\section{References}\label{references}

The cited Pandoc and Quarto records are resolved from the governed
bibliography declared by the pinned toolchain contract; an unresolved
citation fails the qualified render.

\section{Required Textbook Chapter
Contract}\label{required-textbook-chapter-contract}

\subsection{Outcome and Authority}\label{outcome-and-authority-1}

TOOLS-D3 defines the public structure that every calculation-level
textbook chapter must satisfy before registration. The contract is
structural and traceability-focused: passing it does not approve an
equation, implementation, dataset, artifact, license, or engineering
use. TOOLS-D4 now registers one verified-unapproved swing and
Rate-of-Closure exemplar; missing markerless authority remains an
explicit blocker rather than an inferred calculation.

Two version identifiers are fixed:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Contract: \texttt{tools-textbook-chapter-contract/1.0.0}
\item
  Registry: \texttt{tools-textbook-chapter-registry/1.0.0}
\end{itemize}

Their repository-owned JSON Schemas allow external consumers to validate
shape without importing producer code. The Python consumer then applies
stricter invariants for normalized paths, ordering, uniqueness,
authority state, and QMD content.

\subsection{Required Chapter Anatomy}\label{required-chapter-anatomy}

Fourteen ordered sections are mandatory. A registered chapter must
present, in order: Purpose and Scope; Design by Contract; Coordinates,
Frames, and Time; Units and Dimensions; Derivation and Assumptions;
Algorithm; Implementation Symbols; Error and Failure Semantics;
Uncertainty and Sensitivity; Verification and Validation; Limits and
Applicability; Worked Examples; References and Provenance; and Revision
History.

The contract also declares mandatory third-level headings. For example,
Design by Contract requires Preconditions, Postconditions, and
Invariants. Coordinates requires frame, handedness, and time
declarations. Verification and Validation requires test evidence and
acceptance criteria. Exact ordered headings remove format-dependent
inference and make an omitted obligation a deterministic failure.

\subsection{Registration and
Traceability}\label{registration-and-traceability}

Each registered chapter has one stable chapter ID and one normalized QMD
path. Its descriptor binds the chapter version and provisional authority
to an owner, review owner, stable calculation IDs, module IDs,
verification tests, source citations, explicit limitations, and revision
history. All traceability arrays are non-empty, unique, and sorted;
duplicate chapter IDs or paths are rejected.

An \texttt{approved} chapter claim is unsupported by this D3 contract
because later subepics own page, accessibility, publication, and
human-review evidence. D3 accepts only \texttt{provisional} and
\texttt{verified-unapproved} chapter descriptors. The manual and every
generated representation therefore remain \texttt{generated-unapproved}.

\subsection{Linter Algorithm and
Evidence}\label{linter-algorithm-and-evidence}

The linter loads the contract and registry through strict typed
consumers, resolves each registered path beneath
\texttt{manuals/tools/chapters}, decodes UTF-8, and rejects forbidden
placeholder or private-source tokens. It extracts level-2 and level-3
headings, compares them with the exact ordered contract, and checks that
every required section has governed body content.

For normalized chapter text \(T\) and ordered section blocks \(S_i\),
the linter records deterministic evidence as

\[
h_T = \operatorname{SHA256}(\operatorname{LF}(T)), \qquad
h_i = \operatorname{SHA256}(\operatorname{LF}(S_i)).
\]

These hashes detect byte-level content drift while remaining independent
of Windows or POSIX checkout line endings. They are lint evidence, not
scientific approval or an immutable publication digest.

\subsection{Failure and Ownership
Boundaries}\label{failure-and-ownership-boundaries}

Missing files, invalid UTF-8, unsafe paths, unknown fields or versions,
duplicate identities, unsorted traceability, missing or reordered
headings, empty governed content, placeholders, private-source
references, unsupported status promotion, and stale generated artifacts
all fail closed. The linter does not synthesize equations, units,
sources, examples, tests, or limitations.

TOOLS-D4 owns exemplar chapter registration and its fail-closed
dependency coverage. TOOLS-D5 expands phased module coverage, TOOLS-D6
owns executable freshness, TOOLS-D7 owns rendered and accessibility
review, and TOOLS-D8 owns immutable public projection and human
approval.

\subsection{Consumer Workflow}\label{consumer-workflow}

Authors edit only canonical QMD and the machine-readable chapter
registry. Run these commands in order:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{python\ -m} \texttt{scripts.lint\_tools\_textbook\_chapters}
\item
  \texttt{python\ -m} \texttt{scripts.check\_tools\_exemplars}
\item
  \texttt{python\ -m} \texttt{scripts.render\_tools\_design\_manual}
  \texttt{-\/-render}
\end{enumerate}

\section{Swing and Rate-of-Closure D-Plane
Geometry}\label{swing-rate-of-closure-d-plane-exemplar}

\subsection{Purpose and Scope}\label{purpose-and-scope}

This governed exemplar explains how \texttt{swing\_sim} computes
frame-explicit three-dimensional D-plane geometry and how Rate of
Closure supplies three distinct rigid-body velocity points to that
calculation. It is for developers, scientific reviewers, and integrators
who need to reproduce the equations and follow every value into code and
tests. It covers geometric direction relationships only. It does not
predict ball launch, spin magnitude, aerodynamic flight, player outcome,
equipment quality, or an operating decision. The calculation and
rendered artifacts are verified-unapproved.

\subsection{Design by Contract}\label{design-by-contract}

\subsubsection{Preconditions}\label{preconditions}

\texttt{analyze\_dplane} accepts travel, face-normal, target, and up
vectors with exactly three finite components. Face normal, target, and
up must each have Euclidean norm greater than \(10^{-12}\). Target and
up must be orthogonal to absolute dot product \(10^{-10}\). The
Rate-of-Closure adapter additionally requires a typed
\texttt{SimulationRun} with increasing sample times and internally
consistent pose, twist, club, scenario, and inspection-event records.

\subsubsection{Postconditions}\label{postconditions}

Every available direction is normalized and every angle is in degrees.
Spin loft is the principal angle on \([0,180]\). A defined D-plane
supplies a unit normal perpendicular to travel and face. Zero, parallel,
antiparallel, and unprojectable states return explicit status or null
fields; they never invent a plane, horizontal heading, or face-to-path
result.

\subsubsection{Invariants}\label{invariants}

A common proper rotation of travel, face, target, and up preserves spin
loft, planar spin loft, face-to-path, and intrinsic tilt. Reflecting the
right axis reverses signed horizontal relationships while preserving
spin loft. Multiplying a nonzero travel vector by a positive scalar does
not change the geometry because only direction enters the method.

\subsection{Coordinates, Frames, and
Time}\label{coordinates-frames-and-time}

\subsubsection{Coordinate Frames}\label{coordinate-frames}

\protect\phantomsection\label{dplane-coordinate-frame}{}

The default application frame is
\texttt{app\_frame:x\_target,y\_up,z\_right}. Let \(\hat{\mathbf t}\) be
target and \(\hat{\mathbf u}\) be up. The implementation constructs
right as

\[
\hat{\mathbf r} =
  \frac{\hat{\mathbf t}\times\hat{\mathbf u}}
       {\lVert\hat{\mathbf t}\times\hat{\mathbf u}\rVert}.
\]

Rate of Closure interpolates the inspection-event rigid transform and
twist, then expresses reference, face-center, and contact vectors in
this same frame.

\subsubsection{Axis and Handedness}\label{axis-and-handedness}

Positive path and face headings rotate from target toward right.
Elevation is positive toward up. Target-times-up fixes the sign of
right; reversing the cross-product order would reverse every signed
horizontal result. The D-plane normal is travel-times-face, so its
orientation also depends on declared order.

\subsubsection{Time Convention}\label{time-convention}

The geometry is instantaneous and has no integration clock. Rate of
Closure evaluates it at \texttt{inspection\_time\_s}. Pose and twist are
interpolated to that event time; the closest sampled index is audit
metadata and a bounded tangent fallback. A miss remains a
closest-approach event and is not relabeled impact.

\subsection{Units and Dimensions}\label{units-and-dimensions}

\subsubsection{Symbol and Unit Table}\label{symbol-and-unit-table}

\(\mathbf v\) & reference, face-center, or contact velocity & m/s \\

\(\hat{\mathbf t},\hat{\mathbf u},\hat{\mathbf r}\) & target, up, right

\end{longtable}
}

\subsubsection{Dimensional Checks}\label{dimensional-checks}

Normalizing \(\mathbf v\) divides m/s by m/s, producing a unit
direction. Dot and cross products operate on dimensionless directions.
\texttt{acos} and \texttt{atan2} return dimensionless radians, converted
to degrees. The rigid-body equation
\(\mathbf v_P=\mathbf v_O+\boldsymbol\omega\times\mathbf r_{OP}\) is
consistent: rad/s is treated as \(1/s\), and multiplying by metres
produces m/s.

\subsection{Derivation and
Assumptions}\label{derivation-and-assumptions}

\subsubsection{Assumptions}\label{assumptions}

The calculation assumes Euclidean three-space, a right-handed
orthonormal target frame, finite floating-point inputs, and one
instantaneous delivered face normal. It treats the D-plane as geometry
spanned by travel and face; collision dynamics and aerodynamic response
lie outside this method. Rate of Closure assumes its interpolated
homogeneous pose is rigid and its twist stores angular components
followed by translational components.

\subsubsection{Derivation}\label{derivation}

Normalize travel and face as
\(\hat{\mathbf v}=\mathbf v/\lVert\mathbf v\rVert\) and
\(\hat{\mathbf n}=\mathbf n/\lVert\mathbf n\rVert\). Their dot product
is the cosine of the included angle. Clipping protects \texttt{acos}
from roundoff beyond the mathematical interval.

\protect\phantomsection\label{dplane-spin-loft-equation}{}

\[
\lambda = \frac{180}{\pi}
  \cos^{-1}\!\left(
    \operatorname{clip}(\hat{\mathbf v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf n},-1,1)
  \right).
\]

When the vectors are not collinear, the oriented plane normal is

\protect\phantomsection\label{dplane-normal-equation}{}

\[
\hat{\mathbf d} =
  \frac{\hat{\mathbf v}\times\hat{\mathbf n}}
       {\lVert\hat{\mathbf v}\times\hat{\mathbf n}\rVert}.
\]

For any direction \(\mathbf q\), remove its vertical component:
\(\mathbf q_h=\mathbf q-(\mathbf q\cdot\hat{\mathbf u})\hat{\mathbf u}\).
Heading and elevation are
\(\operatorname{atan2}(\mathbf q_h\cdot\hat{\mathbf r},
\mathbf q_h\cdot\hat{\mathbf t})\) and
\(\operatorname{atan2}(\mathbf q\cdot\hat{\mathbf u},
\lVert\mathbf q_h\rVert)\). Face-to-path wraps \(f-p\) to
\([-180,180)\). Rate of Closure obtains face-center velocity from
rigid-body kinematics before applying the same geometry.

\subsection{Algorithm}\label{algorithm}

\subsubsection{Inputs}\label{inputs}

The standalone calculation consumes \texttt{travel\_vector},
\texttt{face\_normal}, optional \texttt{target} and \texttt{up}, and
descriptive \texttt{frame\_id}. The consumer accepts one immutable
\texttt{SimulationRun} and derives inspection pose, twist, shaft
geometry, contact lever, face normal, leading-edge tangent, and arc
tangent rather than asking callers to assemble those values.

\subsubsection{Procedure}\label{procedure}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Convert each vector to a finite three-component array and validate the
  frame.
\item
  Normalize face, target, and up; derive right from target-times-up.
\item
  Compute face heading and dynamic loft even if travel is zero.
\item
  Return \texttt{zero\_travel} when travel norm is at most \(10^{-12}\).
\item
  Normalize travel; compute path, attack, face-to-path, and spin loft.
\item
  Return \texttt{parallel} or \texttt{antiparallel} for a singular cross
  product.
\item
  Otherwise derive plane normal, tilt, inclination, and ground
  intersection.
\item
  Rate of Closure repeats the calculation for reference, face center,
  and contact so a consumer cannot silently confuse those datums.
\end{enumerate}

Standalone work is constant time and memory. Sector rendering is linear
in the caller-bounded segment count and returns \texttt{segments\ +\ 1}
unit directions.

\subsubsection{Outputs}\label{outputs}

\texttt{DPlaneAnalysis} returns status, frame, normalized basis vectors,
optional plane and ground-intersection directions, three-dimensional and
planar spin loft, residual, path, attack, face, dynamic loft,
face-to-path, azimuth, tilt, and inclination.
\texttt{ImpactKinematicSnapshot} wraps three analyses with event,
geometry basis, limitations, pose, and wedge-kinematics evidence.

\subsection{Implementation Symbols}\label{implementation-symbols}

\subsubsection{Public Symbols}\label{public-symbols}

The stable \texttt{shared.python.swing\_sim.impact} facade exports
\texttt{DPlaneStatus}, \texttt{DPlaneAnalysis},
\texttt{analyze\_dplane}, and \texttt{spin\_loft\_sector\_directions}.
Rate of Closure exports \texttt{ImpactKinematicSnapshot} and
\texttt{impact\_kinematics\_for\_run}. Consumers should not import
private helpers such as \texttt{\_heading\_deg} or
\texttt{\_shaft\_geometry}.

\subsubsection{Source Mapping}\label{source-mapping}

Calculation \texttt{TOOLS-DPLANE-GEOMETRY} maps spin loft, normal,
heading, elevation, singular states, and sectors to
\texttt{src/shared/python/swing\_sim/impact/dplane.py}. The
Rate-of-Closure datum and point-velocity mapping lives in
\texttt{src/rate\_of\_closure/simulation/impact\_kinematics.py}. Both
are pinned to D3 base \texttt{916fb9f27f486486f0c071dcc6f15f81f68ecb18};
their provisional module IDs and public symbols remain recorded in the
module inventory.

\subsection{Error and Failure
Semantics}\label{error-and-failure-semantics}

\subsubsection{Error Conditions}\label{error-conditions}

Wrong vector shape, non-finite values, zero face/target/up, or a
nonorthogonal frame raises \texttt{ValueError}. A
non-\texttt{SimulationRun} input raises \texttt{TypeError}.
Nonincreasing times, zero shaft geometry, zero path fallback, or
degenerate projected leading edge also fail preconditions. These
failures are distinct from valid singular geometry.

\subsubsection{Recovery and
Cancellation}\label{recovery-and-cancellation}

Callers recover by correcting source data or frame; the method does not
coerce, interpolate missing vectors, or substitute a default. Valid
singular statuses may be displayed with null fields intact. The
synchronous calculation is bounded and has no external I/O, so it has no
mid-operation cancellation seam. Higher-level cancellation occurs before
calls or between complete runs.

\subsection{Uncertainty and
Sensitivity}\label{uncertainty-and-sensitivity}

\subsubsection{Uncertainty Sources}\label{uncertainty-sources}

The implementation does not estimate covariance. Uncertainty can enter
through travel, face orientation, coordinate transform, event
interpolation, club geometry, or the choice of reference versus contact
datum. Floating-point clipping addresses numerical roundoff only; it is
not a measurement uncertainty model. Angles therefore remain
model-conditioned rather than observed truth.

\subsubsection{Sensitivity}\label{sensitivity}

Small perturbations are smooth away from singular states. Sensitivity
rises when horizontal projection approaches zero because heading becomes
undefined, and when travel and face approach parallel or antiparallel
because a small cross product cannot define a stable normal. The API
exposes these limits as null or typed status; downstream code must not
carry forward a prior frame's plane.

\subsection{Verification and
Validation}\label{verification-and-validation}

\subsubsection{Test Evidence}\label{test-evidence}

\texttt{test\_matches\_cross\_client\_golden\_contract} executes three
analytical cases from \texttt{dplane\_golden\_v1.json} at absolute
tolerance \(10^{-9}\) degree. Singular-state tests cover zero travel,
parallel, antiparallel, vertical projection, and invalid frames.
Rotation and reflection tests pin invariants. The Rate-of-Closure
integration test derives face-center velocity independently as
\(\mathbf v_O+\boldsymbol\omega\times\mathbf r\), then proves the
consumer normalizes that value for its face-center D-plane.

\subsubsection{Acceptance Criteria}\label{acceptance-criteria}

The exemplar passes only when strict JSON Schema and typed loader agree;
calculation, chapter, module, source, consumer, test, and golden-fixture
links all resolve; the fourteen-section linter and focused tests pass;
and HTML, LaTeX, PDF, and DOCX share the governed semantic digest. This
evidence verifies reproduction, not scientific or publication approval.

\subsection{Limits and Applicability}\label{limits-and-applicability}

\subsubsection{Validity Range}\label{validity-range}

Finite vectors may have any representable scale, but face and frame axes
must exceed norm \(10^{-12}\), and target/up orthogonality must satisfy
\(10^{-10}\). Spin loft spans \(0\) through \(180\) degrees. Signed
relationships wrap to \([-180,180)\). The golden fixture qualifies only
its declared cases and \(10^{-9}\)-degree tolerance.

\subsubsection{Known Limitations}\label{known-limitations}

The method does not compute ball response, impulse, spin rate, lift,
drag, landing, biomechanics, or camera-derived pose. It does not
establish that an external device's axes, timestamps, or face normal
match this contract. Rate of Closure downstream flight currently
consumes reference-point translation; shaft-induced contact velocity
remains analysis. The markerless-mocap exemplar is deliberately absent
because TOOLS-M0 issue \#4708 and PR \#4734 are open and no markerless
module exists on this D3 base. Unmerged content is not promoted.

\subsection{Worked Examples}\label{worked-examples}

\subsubsection{Example Inputs}\label{example-inputs}

The governed \texttt{square-descending} fixture supplies
\(\mathbf v=(0.9986295347545738,-0.052335956242943835,0)\), with path
\(0^\circ\) and attack \(-3^\circ\). Its face normal is
\(\mathbf n=(0.9781476007338057,0.20791169081775934,0)\), with face
\(0^\circ\) and dynamic loft \(12^\circ\). Target and up use default
unit axes. The fixture tolerance is \(10^{-9}\) degree.

\subsubsection{Example Results}\label{example-results}

The dot product is \(\cos 15^\circ\), so spin loft is \(15^\circ\).
Dynamic loft minus attack is \(12-(-3)=15^\circ\), making planar
residual zero. Travel-times-face points along right, giving
\(\hat{\mathbf d}=(0,0,1)\), tilt \(0^\circ\), inclination \(90^\circ\),
and ground intersection at \(0^\circ\). Status is \texttt{defined}.
Values come from the cross-client golden fixture and executable Python
test, not renderer-only text.
